title: 08. GraphRAG: Graph RAG Foundations
summary: Graph RAG (Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation) augments LLM generation by retrieving context from a structured knowledge graph rather than (or in addition to) a flat vector index.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: **Graph RAG (Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation)** augments LLM generation by retrieving context from a **structured knowledge graph** rather than (or in addition to) a flat vector index. In naive RAG, documents are chunked, embedded, and retrieved by semantic similarity — meaning the system has no awareness of *how* entities relate to each other across documents. Graph RAG solves this by first constructing a knowledge graph of entities and relationships from the corpus, then performing **graph-aware retrieval** (subgraph extraction, community summarisation, multi-hop traversal) before passing context to the LLM. The core motivation is that many real-world questions are **relational** — "Which companies co-founded by the same investor later competed?" — and cannot be answered by similarity search alone. Microsoft's GraphRAG paper (2024) showed that global sensemaking queries (questions that require synthesising information across many documents) were dramatically better answered by Graph RAG than by naive RAG or even advanced RAG.

diagrams.title: GraphRAG: build a knowledge graph, then retrieve from it
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  subgraph IDX["Indexing"]
    T["text chunks"] --> EX["LLM extracts entities + relations"] --> KG[("knowledge graph")]
    KG --> CM["community detection"] --> SUM["community summaries"]
  end
  subgraph QRY["Querying"]
    Q["question"] --> LOC["local search — entity + neighbours"]
    Q --> GLO["global search — map-reduce over summaries"]
  end
  KG --> LOC
  SUM --> GLO
diagrams.explain: Vector RAG finds *similar passages*; GraphRAG captures **who is connected to what**. Entities and relations become a graph; communities of related entities get summaries. **Local search** answers questions about specific entities; **global search** answers "what are the main themes?" questions that no single chunk can.

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
                    GRAPH RAG vs NAIVE RAG — ARCHITECTURE COMPARISON

  NAIVE RAG                              GRAPH RAG
  ┌─────────────────────────┐           ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │      INDEXING            │           │           INDEXING                    │
  │                          │           │                                        │
  │  Documents               │           │  Documents                             │
  │      │                   │           │      │                                 │
  │      ▼                   │           │      ▼                                 │
  │  [Chunk 1][Chunk 2]...   │           │  Text Units → NER/LLM Extraction      │
  │      │                   │           │      │                                 │
  │      ▼                   │           │      ▼                                 │
  │  [Embed] [Embed] ...     │           │  (Entity, Relation, Entity) Triples   │
  │      │                   │           │      │                                 │
  │      ▼                   │           │      ▼                                 │
  │  Vector Index            │           │  Knowledge Graph                       │
  │  (flat, no structure)    │           │  (nodes + edges + properties)          │
  │                          │           │      │                                 │
  │                          │           │      ▼                                 │
  │                          │           │  Community Detection (Leiden)          │
  │                          │           │      │                                 │
  │                          │           │      ▼                                 │
  │                          │           │  Community Reports (LLM summaries)    │
  └─────────────────────────┘           └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  QUERY TIME                             QUERY TIME
  ┌─────────────────────────┐           ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Query                  │           │  Query                                 │
  │    │                    │           │    │                                   │
  │    ▼                    │           │    ▼                                   │
  │  Embed Query            │           │  Entity Extraction (NER)              │
  │    │                    │           │    │                                   │
  │    ▼                    │           │    ▼                                   │
  │  Cosine Similarity      │           │  Entity Linking → Graph Nodes         │
  │    │                    │           │    │                                   │
  │    ▼                    │           │    ├── LOCAL: k-hop traversal          │
  │  Top-K Chunks           │           │    │       → subgraph extraction       │
  │  (semantic proximity    │           │    │       → entity + rel context      │
  │   only, no structure)   │           │    │                                   │
  │    │                    │           │    └── GLOBAL: score all communities   │
  │    ▼                    │           │            → map-reduce synthesis      │
  │  LLM Answer             │           │    │                                   │
  │  (may hallucinate       │           │    ▼                                   │
  │   relationships)        │           │  Context Assembly (layered)           │
  │                         │           │  [Communities][Entities][Relations]    │
  │                         │           │    │                                   │
  │                         │           │    ▼                                   │
  │                         │           │  LLM Answer (grounded in graph)       │
  └─────────────────────────┘           └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  FAILURE MODES                          FAILURE MODES
  ┌─────────────────────────┐           ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ ✗ No relationship aware │           │ ✗ Entity extraction noise (🔍)        │
  │ ✗ Misses cross-doc info │           │ ✗ Community misassignment (🌀)        │
  │ ✗ No thematic synthesis │           │ ✗ Stale graph (🦠)                    │
  │ ✓ Fast, cheap           │           │ ✗ High indexing cost (💸)             │
  │ ✓ Simple to operate     │           │ ✓ Relational queries                  │
  │                         │           │ ✓ Global sensemaking                  │
  └─────────────────────────┘           └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  QUERY TYPE ROUTING
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                                                        │
  │  "What did CEO say?" ──────────────► NAIVE RAG         │
  │                                                        │
  │  "How are A and B connected?" ─────► GRAPH RAG LOCAL   │
  │                                                        │
  │  "What are the main themes?" ──────► GRAPH RAG GLOBAL  │
  │                                                        │
  │  "Find similar docs + relationships" ► HYBRID          │
  │                                                        │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

quiz.question: What is the fundamental architectural difference between naive RAG and Graph RAG at the retrieval layer?
options: The key innovation is hierarchical community summarisation combined with a map-reduce global query engine.
Community reports are pre-computed natural-language summaries of clusters of related entities, generated during indexing.
(1) Text splitting — corpus chunked into overlapping text units.
Naive RAG retrieves top-k document chunks by cosine similarity between query embedding and chunk embeddings — it is a flat, point-in-time lookup.
quiz.explanation: Naive RAG retrieves top-k document chunks by cosine similarity between query embedding and chunk embeddings — it is a flat, point-in-time lookup. Graph RAG retrieves a subgraph (entities + relationships + community summaries) by performing graph traversal from query-linked entities, meaning it captures structural context — the path of relationships between entities — rather than just semantic proximity of text. ---

quiz.question: What are the three layers of context that Graph RAG provides to the LLM that naive RAG cannot?
options: (1) Text splitting — corpus chunked into overlapping text units.
Text units are the fundamental input chunks from which entities and relationships are extracted.
The key innovation is hierarchical community summarisation combined with a map-reduce global query engine.
(2) Relationship-level context — explicit edges between entities (how A is related to B, with relationship type and properties).
quiz.explanation: (1) Entity-level context — structured facts about specific entities (attributes, aliases, descriptions). (2) Relationship-level context — explicit edges between entities (how A is related to B, with relationship type and properties). (3) Community-level context — aggregated summaries of clusters of tightly connected entities, enabling global sensemaking.

quiz.question: Why does naive RAG fail for "What is the overall theme connecting these 500 research papers?
options: (2) Relationship-level context — explicit edges between entities (how A is related to B, with relationship type and properties).
During indexing, entities from all documents are merged into a single unified graph.
Naive RAG assembles context by concatenating the top-k retrieved chunks in similarity-score order, with no awareness of structural relationships.
This is a global sensemaking query — it requires synthesising information across the entire corpus rather than finding a specific passage.
quiz.explanation: This is a global sensemaking query — it requires synthesising information across the entire corpus rather than finding a specific passage. Naive RAG would retrieve 5–10 chunks by similarity, which are necessarily local and biased toward the query embedding.

quiz.question: What is the Graph RAG indexing pipeline and what are its 5 main stages?
options: Text units are the fundamental input chunks from which entities and relationships are extracted.
(2) Relationship-level context — explicit edges between entities (how A is related to B, with relationship type and properties).
Community reports are pre-computed natural-language summaries of clusters of related entities, generated during indexing.
(1) Text splitting — corpus chunked into overlapping text units.
quiz.explanation: (1) Text splitting — corpus chunked into overlapping text units. (2) Entity and relationship extraction — LLM or NER extracts (entity, relation, entity) triples from each chunk. (3) Graph construction — triples assembled into a property graph; entities deduplicated.

quiz.question: What is the key innovation of Microsoft GraphRAG over existing knowledge graph QA systems?
options: Text units are the fundamental input chunks from which entities and relationships are extracted.
(1) Text splitting — corpus chunked into overlapping text units.
(2) Relationship-level context — explicit edges between entities (how A is related to B, with relationship type and properties).
The key innovation is hierarchical community summarisation combined with a map-reduce global query engine.
quiz.explanation: The key innovation is hierarchical community summarisation combined with a map-reduce global query engine. Traditional KGQA systems query graphs via SPARQL/Cypher and return structured facts — they cannot synthesise thematic summaries.
